blocks.text: Wadbhag Singh now dictates the terms in practice, warning Dina Beg to keep his own troops inside camp while the Khalsa enters Jalandhar. The city is subjected to selective vengeance and humiliation against its enemies, and the Nawab is left to prove submission rather than command events.

Once the pressure has done its work, Dina Beg returns with one lakh rupees and karah parshad as a visible acknowledgment of Sikh ascendancy. The money is handed over before the Khalsa, and the sacred offering is distributed in a setting that blends triumph, thanksgiving, and political settlement.

The Nawab even praises the karah parshad as he tastes it, underscoring how far he has moved from bargaining partner to dependent ally. The page closes with cash, ritual, and public deference combining to ratify the Sikh victory at Jalandhar.
